REGRESSED 13 -> 18 words, and this is the informative probe: data_off/track_off moved DOWN to r27/r26 and i/anim_base moved UP to r29/r28, i.e. the declared locals reordered among themselves exactly as declared, while the two compiler-generated address temps stayed at r31/r30. (2) NAMED-TEMP REMOVAL: deleted `s32* count;` and `count = &gWorldInfo.nworldanims;` and wrote `while (i < gWorldInfo.nworldanims)`. 13 words, and the aligned view is BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD's - MWCC rebuilds the same `addi rX,base,144` temp either way, so the named-local-versus-CSE-temp distinction is not a lever here. NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, decisive at one. (3) WIDTH/TYPE: `u8* data_off; u8* track_off;` initialised to NULL and stepped by 160/16 with `(u32)` casts at both use sites -> `s32 data_off; s32 track_off;` initialised to 0 with the casts deleted. 63/63 insns, 13 words, aligned view again BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD. Note for a reconstruction-quality lane: form (3) is byte-equal and is better C than a null pointer incremented by 160 and cast back to u32 - it was reverted here only to keep this lane's diff to the one promotion it landed.
attributes.residual: The rule stays; this record is the source-exhaustion provenance it did not have. THE MECHANISM, from the aligned raw view. Four values live in r28-r31 and both streams define them in the same order: the CSE'd `&gWorldInfo` base (@0x60 target `addi r29,r3,0` against ours `addi r31,r3,0`), the loop-limit address base+144 (@0x64 target `addi r28,r29,144` against ours `addi r30,r31,144`), the 160-stride offset (@0x8c target `li r31,0` against ours `li r29,0`) and the 16-stride offset (@0x90 target `li r30,0` against ours `li r28,0`). `i` (r27) and `anim_base` (r26) agree in every stream and every probe. So ours ranks {base, count} above {data_off, track_off} and retail ranks them the other way round - a rotation by two of a four-element list, with the last two elements pinned. Probe (1) is what makes this a cap rather than a guess: MWCC gives r31 and r30 to the two compiler-generated ADDRESS TEMPS and then hands r29 downwards to the DECLARED locals in declaration order, and moving the declaration list only permutes the locals WITHIN that lower block. Retail's shape needs two declared locals ABOVE the two address temps, which no permutation of the declaration list can express, because the block boundary is not a declaration-order fact.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Count the callee-saved registers each stream actually uses. If retail uses SIX (r26-r31) and ours uses six, no web is being eliminated and any 'stop creating the temp' lever must show up as an instruction-count change, which would contradict 63/63. Measured 2026-09-03: both streams use exactly r26-r31 and both are 63 instructions, so the eliminate-a-web reading is WRONG and the surviving form of the hypothesis is the ranking one - some property of retail's source made the two address temps rank below two locals without changing how many webs exist.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the four defining instructions, their offsets and both register assignments were read from the aligned raw view against the retail bytes over the whole 63-instruction body, and the i/anim_base agreement was confirmed in HEAD and in all three probes.
hypothesis.statement: The lever is not on the declared locals at all - it is on the two ADDRESS TEMPS. Retail's build ranked the `&gWorldInfo` and `&gWorldInfo.nworldanims` webs BELOW two declared locals, which our build never does for a temp created at the top of the guarded block. The untried axis is to stop those temps being created at that point: force the base address to be re-materialised at each use (so no long-lived base web exists and the loop offsets take r31/r30), e.g. by writing the three in-loop global reads as full `gWorldInfo.<member>` expressions inside a scope that does not share the guard's base, or by moving the `header`/`anim_base` reads into the loop preheader so the base web dies before the offsets are initialised.
